title: Accuracy of Static Surgical Guides by Support Type: A Narrative Review of Tooth-, Mucosa- and Bone-Supported Guides
content: Background: Static computer-assisted implant surgery (s-CAIS) transfers a virtual implant plan to the patient through a surgical guide. The tissue that supports the guide (teeth, mucosa or bone) is one of the main factors that determines how closely the placed implant matches the plan. Objective: To summarise the clinical evidence on the accuracy of tooth-, mucosa- and bone-supported static surgical guides and to translate it into practical guide selection considerations. Methods: Narrative review of systematic reviews, meta-analyses and comparative clinical studies published between 2017 and 2026 that reported coronal (entry), apical and angular deviation between planned and placed implant positions according to guide support type. Results: Pooled data place the overall mean error of s-CAIS at about 1.1 to 1.2 mm at the entry point, 1.4 mm at the apex and 3.5 degrees in angulation. Tooth-supported guides were the most accurate support type in most comparisons. Bone-supported guides showed greater deviation than tooth-supported guides in two meta-analyses, while a recent retrospective clinical comparison of 180 implants found an accuracy gradient of tooth, then bone, then mucosa support. In fully edentulous mandibles, mucosa-supported guides produced the largest deviations in one retrospective multicentre series. Fully guided protocols were more accurate than pilot-drill protocols. Conclusions: Guide support type influences implant placement accuracy, but every support type delivered mean deviations within commonly accepted clinical limits. Guide selection should follow the remaining dentition, arch, soft tissue condition and surgical protocol, with a safety margin of at least 2 mm from critical anatomical structures.
